title: Programming MOF Topology through Twelve-Connected Linker Isomerism
abstract: Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Context-Aware Framework for Biological Health Index Harmonization and Machine Learning-Aided Health Forecasting of Waterbodies
abstract: National biological monitoring repositories, such as the U.S. EPA’s STORET/WQX, accumulate ecological health scores of water bodies from many agencies using heterogeneous biological indices and scoring conventions. Due to the different standards these agencies adhere to, these scores are not directly comparable. This difference in health score scales and benchmarks undermines large-scale ecological analysis and the application of machine learning models to forecast waterbody health.

title: Cancers relax selection on charge at the mitochondrial complex I quinone cavity
abstract: Mitochondrial complex I translocates protons through hydrated channels whose connectivity and electrostatics are both defined by structure, but whether they are distinctly constrained is unknown. From a 2.39 cryo-EM structure modelling 2,945 ordered waters, we built the proton wire of the seven mtDNA-encoded ND subunits and scored all 40,166 missense substitutions on two near-orthogonal axes (r = 0.17): electrostatic shift at proton-loading sites, and topological disruption of the wire. Across 858 germline variant sites, loading sites (0.51) and cut vertices (0.67) are both depleted.

title: Adsorption of cations at electrochemical interfaces revisited
abstract: At electrochemical interfaces, alkali-metal and alkaline-earth metal cations are usually described as solvated species that nonspecifically adsorb, whereas specifically adsorbed anions interact more directly with metal electrodes. However, the mode of cation-surface interaction remains poorly defined at the atomic scale because experiments typically measure averaged interfacial responses. Distinguishing hydration modulated polarization from localized ion-surface coupling therefore requires access to both the atomic structure and the redistribution of electronic charge.

title: Can existing or future pathways reduce green ammonia production costs?
abstract: Many scenarios for the energy transition consider green ammonia. The technologically most mature production process combines water electrolysis and Haber-Bosch process (EHB). Its costs are dominated by electrolyzer investment costs and electricity. Emerging pathways researched in academia, start-ups, and industry try to reduce costs by changing sub-processes and chemistry. However, it remains unclear which pathways have the potential to outperform EHB, if any. We assess relevant emerging pathways, compare to EHB in terms of costs and energy demand, and derive performance targets.

title: Enzymatic Conversion from a Vicinal Diol to a Vicinal Diketone: Computational Study of the Conserved 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin-Forming Stage in Mammalian and Bacterial PTPS
abstract: As a zinc- and magnesium-dependent triphosphatase, 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (PTPS) catalyzes the conversion of dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin (PPH4) and a triphosphate ion, representing a typical reaction for vicinal diketone biosynthesis from vicinal diol. The molecular mechanism of PTPS remains elusive owing to the lack of structural data containing native substrate H2NTP and magnesium ion.

title: Synthesis of zigzag-type carbocationic nanobelts
abstract: Belt[n]arenes correspond the shortest belt segments of zigzag carbon nanotubes. Their closed cyclic π-conjugated topologies and distinct size-dependent electronic configurations render them platforms for the construction of quantum materials and devices. Here, we report the synthesis of a fully conjugated carbocationic zigzag-type belt consisting of four linearly fused benzotropylium units. Belt[4]arene[4]tropylium salt was synthesized from resorcin[4]arene via a sequence featuring fjord-stitching olefin metathesis reactions, selective bromination and heterolytic C–Br bond cleavage reaction.

title: DFT Studies of Coherent States in Triphenylamine Trimers
abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations were performed to investigate the degree of coherence in two triphenylamine trimers: restricted and unrestricted. The B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level of theory was employed in this study. Toluene and dichloromethane were used as solvents to understand the effects of the solvent environment on the properties of the trimers. The unrestricted trimer exhibits a larger HOMO-LUMO energy gap and a shorter absorption wavelength than the restricted trimer, indicating a lower degree of coherence.

title: Framework-Templated Single Clathrate Hydrate Cages in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Molecular simulations identify metal–organic framework (MOF) pores that retain single methane hydrate cages and, for a nonstandard 16-water cage, support its assembly from disordered water. In smooth spherical pores, a methane molecule assembled twenty waters into the pentagonal dodecahedron of structure I hydrate and sixteen waters into a 435661 cage, a polyhedron that no known hydrate crystal contains.

title: Electrolyte-derived interphases control nonuniform charging in battery particle networks
abstract: In an ensemble of battery particles, dynamic interactions among individual particles give rise to emergent behavior like nonuniform charging. Yet, its origins have remained contested due to the challenge of directly measuring the current into each particle. Inspired by neuronal potential recordings in brain-computer interfaces, we present Multichannel Acquisition of Parallel-particle Level Electrochemistry (MAPLE) to map dynamic current distributions in real time.

title: A General Approach for the Generation of alpha-Thioalkyl Radicals from Pinacol Boronic Ester Precursors
abstract: A straightforward and effective method to produce alpha-thioalkyl radicals using stable and readily accessible pinacol boronic ester precursors is described. The generation of alpha-thioalkyl radicals proceeds via in-situ transesterification with MeOBcat or 3-methoxycatechol (MOC), and subsequent nucleohomolytic substitution at the boron atom with an oxygen-centred radical. The alpha-thioalkyl radicals can be trapped intermolecularly using a variety of conjugated enones and sulfonyl-based radical traps or subjected to intramolecular cyclisation.

title: Selective Adsorption Processes in Mordenite-Catalysed Ethanol Dehydration
abstract: Ethanol dehydration offers a promising solution to improve the sustainability of ethene production, using biomass-derived feedstocks and a heavy-metal-free zeolite catalyst. To improve understanding of the key chemical steps in this reaction, the adsorption of key species in acid-catalysed ethanol dehydration have been investigated on Brønsted Acid (BA) sites in protonated mordenite (MOR).

title: Probing ionomer distribution in PEMFC catalyst layers: AFM and DEM enabled microstructure analysis
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) catalyst layers have been probed experimentally and theoretically for decades. However, existing microscopy techniques lack the ability to perform quantitative analyses on the catalyst and ionomer distributions of catalyst layers. Since the microstructure of the catalyst layer has an influence on the electrochemical performance, the simulation of catalyst layer microstructures is of great importance. A physics-based simulation model was recently reported to predict the microstructure of the catalyst layer as a function of ink composition.

title: Reference Conventions and Structure Types, Rather Than 4f Occupancy, Shape Lanthanide Errors in Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Compounds that pair a lanthanide with a d-block metal and a p-block anion sit behind permanent magnets, catalysts and energy-storage materials, yet large parts of this chemical space have not been computed. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials now make it possible to screen such spaces for stability at a small fraction of the cost of density functional theory, and they are increasingly used to decide which candidates are worth calculating properly.

title: A General Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxidative Radical-Polar Crossover Platform for Secondary and Primary Alkyl Radicals
abstract: Along with recent advances in photoredox-mediated radical generation, oxidative radical–polar crossover (ORPC), involving single-electron oxidation of an alkyl radical to the corresponding carbocation, has emerged as a promising strategy for carbocation generation without use of strong acid mediators. However, current photoredox-mediated ORPC systems are not applicable to secondary and primary alkyl radicals due to their short lifetimes and high oxidation potentials, thereby hampering the development of general synthetic platforms for radical/cation-mediated alkylation of heteroatom…

title: Anti-Parallel Dimer Structure of p-Cyanophenol Adsorbed at the Aqueous Solution Surface Probed by Sub-1 cm-1 High Resolution
abstract: Sub-1 cm-1 High Resolution Broadband Sum-Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectra (HR-BB-SFG-VS) in different polarization combinations and experimental configurations was used to measure the spectral lineshape in the -CN stretching vibration region of p-cyanophenol (PCP) molecules at the air/water interface. The HR-BB-SFG-VS with a spectral resolution of ~ 0.6 cm-1 provides accurate and nearly intrinsic SFG spectral lineshape with excellent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

title: Foldability Is an Intrinsic Property of Protein Sequences: A Lattice Model Study with Information-Theoretic Approach and Unsupervised Machine Learning
abstract: Protein structure prediction has been largely solved, but why a given sequence is foldable has not. We address this question for 27-, 48- and 64-residue lattice heteropolymers with statistical thermodynamics, the informationtheoretic approach (ITA) and a variational autoencoder (VAE). Native populations, folding probabilities and freeenergy surfaces are reproducible and independent of the initial denatured ensemble, so foldability is an intrinsic property of the sequence at a given temperature and solvent. We then ask where the observed regularities come from.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Mixture-Design for Multi-Oxide Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glass Development: Model Comparison, Modifier Interactions, and Predictive Limitations
abstract: A constrained ternary mixture design (Design of Experiments, DoE) was applied to four magnesium aluminosilicate (MAS) glass series to evaluate the predictive capability of Scheffé mixture polynomials for the specific Young’s modulus (spE = E/ρ), the key figure of merit for lightweight glass-fibre reinforcements. Two base compositions (V, Al2O3-rich; T, MgO-rich) were each modified with a 14 wt.% Y2O3–ZnO–CeO2 or La2O3–ZnO–CeO2 block. Linear, quadratic and special-cubic models were fitted to ten design points per series and ranked by R2, R2(adj) and the leave-one-out coefficient R2(pred).

title: A Molecular View of the Osmotic Response of Polyelectrolyte Complex Coacervates
abstract: Synthetic polyelectrolyte complex coacervates are a ubiquitous class of liquid–liquid phase-separated (LLPS) systems that closely mimic the dynamic condensates often seen in cellular environments, where macromolecular crowding fundamentally shapes their physicochemical properties and biological function. For synthetic systems, neutral crowding agents, such as poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), enhance coacervation, although the direct impact of osmotic stress on the structural and thermodynamic stability of the dense coacervate phase remains incompletely understood.

title: Polariton-Mediated Electron Transfer Rate Constant from Non-Equilibrium Fermi’s Golden Rule
abstract: We provide a time-domain derivation of the population transfer rates for the polariton-mediated electron transfer (PMET) reaction under the collective coupling regime. Our theoretical analysis leads to the corresponding Marcus theory rates under the high-temperature and Markovian bath approximations. In addition to including the non-Markovian effect and the low-temperature limits, the theory is also generalized to include the multiple donor-to-acceptor case, as well as including multiple cavity modes.

title: Cellulosic fibers coated in mineral sheaths for flame-retardant nonwovens
abstract: While plant-based materials composed of cellulosic fibers have a favorable sustainability profile in several respects compared to synthetic alternatives, they are flammable and often require treatment for safe use. Many traditional flame-retardant finishes are toxic, while others are difficult to integrate with fibers or fabrics. In this work, cellulosic fibers (cotton, lyocell, jute, and hemp) were coated with crystalline calcite (calcium carbonate) or gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) using a “polymer-induced liquid precursor” strategy.

title: One-Electron Modulation of Photophysics in a Through-Space Donor–Acceptor System
abstract: Through-space donor–acceptor interactions provide an attractive strategy for controlling molecular electronic structures and excited-state properties. However, the influence of one-electron transformations on the photophysical behavior of such systems remains relatively unexplored. Herein, we report an isolable carbazole–xanthylium cation (5+) and its corresponding neutral radical (5•), in which the donor and acceptor units are held in close spatial proximity.

title: Electronic Descriptors Lower Oxygen-Vacancy Formation-Energy Error Relative to Crystal Structure Alone in Non-Magnetic Oxides
abstract: Oxygen vacancies control conduction, catalysis and ion transport in oxides, and an error of 0.3 eV in their neutral formation energy changes their concentration at 1000 K thirty-fold. Graph networks predict this energy from structure alone, but whether electronic descriptors of the pristine host from density-functional theory help is untested at matched training oxides. We compared a structure-only network (S) with one also given 22 such descriptors (D) on 1726 vacancy sites in 818 non-magnetic oxides of the Kumagai database, testing on unseen formulas.

title: Charged Interface in Battery Breaks Molecular Chiral Symmetry
abstract: Molecular events occurring within a few solvent layers at a charged electrode surface govern the rate and reversibility of reactions in electrochemical devices, yet such interfacial mechanism was never sufficiently understood at atomistic-level. Here we report a counter-intuitive discovery that charged interface breaks down the mirror symmetry between R - and S -enantiomers of propylene carbonate (PC), which expresses at graphite surface into distinct interphasial chemistries.

title: Chiral H2S Ice
abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking and the emergence of homochirality have been long-standing mysteries in chemistry and physics. The observation of symmetry breaking in simple triatomic molecules, such as hydrogen sulfide (H2S), is challenging owing to rapid molecular motion and structural relaxation, it provides a fundamental yet poorly understood pathway to molecular handedness in the prebiotic universe.We reportthe firstexperimentalcharacterization of emergent chirality in H2S clusters using vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) in cryogenic matrices (4–40 K).

title: Tailored Nitrone [3+2] Dipolar Cycloaddition Enables the Elusive Synthesis of Structurally Complex Seven-Membered Heterocycles
abstract: Intramolecular [3+2] nitrone cycloadditions have seldom been used to construct 7-membered heterocycles as the formation of the competing 6-membered heterocycles is favored almost exclusively. Herein, we report an intramolecular nitrone cycloaddition that proceeds with a strong preference for the formation of seven-membered 2-benzazepines. The reaction tolerates electronically diverse substrates, including heterocyclic variants, delivering a variety of structurally diverse and synthetically challenging 2-benzazepines in yields up to 76% with diastereomeric ratios up to 20:1.

title: Isolable silyl- and germyl-thioketones dearomatize their own benzene rings at room temperature
abstract: Although dearomatization of benzene converts flat molecules into three-dimensional (3D) frameworks, the stability of the benzene ring makes this transformation difficult. Main-group compounds that achieve it are typically highly reactive low-valent species or contain weak multiple bonds and usually require elaborate design. Thioketones engage an adjacent aryl ring only with strongly electron-poor partners or fused arenes, and the products rearomatize.

title: Correcting the Liquid Densities of Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Using Local-Number-Density Repulsion
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) such as UMA, trained on reference data from meta-generalized gradient approximation or hybrid functionals that incorporate dispersion interactions, often overestimate molecular-liquid densities, thereby placing every property computed at constant pressure at the wrong state point. This study proposes a correction that adds to the MLIP a repulsive energy quadratic in the local number density of each atom, with two coefficients fitted only to the equations of state of water and ethanol; the forces and stresses follow analytically, so…

title: SKIER: A Scientific Skills Framework for Evidence-Grounded AI Reasoning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to interpret experiments and propose mechanisms, but its mechanistic claims often lack traceable evidence. Here we introduce SKIER (Skills for Evidence-grounded AI Reasoning), a scientific skills AI framework that combines AI orchestration, researcher-defined analytical procedures, deterministic calculations, and versioned records.

title: Direct Synthesis of CdSe Quantum Dot Inks in Polar Solvents with Conductive Ligands
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) have unlocked advancements in technologies like displays and light detectors, thanks to their tuneable photoelectronic properties and scalability. However, several device schemes based on electronically conducting QD layers, such as photodetectors and LEDs, require processing QDs as concentrated inks with short, conductive ligands. Currently, this is only achievable after replacing the insulating ligands used during their colloidal synthesis, a process that is both time-consuming and resource-intensive.

title: Advances in OLED Technology: From Fundamental Materials, Device Architectures to Emerging Applications
abstract: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) have emerged as a leading optoelectronic platform, owing to their high efficiency, tunable emission, and mechanical flexibility, yet key questions remain about which molecular design strategies and device architectures are advancing commercial performance, and where persistent bottlenecks, such as blueemitter instability, continue to limit progress, Here, we address these questions through a data-driven analysis of approximately 86 thousand OLED-related documents from the CAS Content CollectionTM spanning 2016–2026, a period chosen to capture recent…

title: (iso-bpy)Ni: Isomeric Bipyridine Ligands in Nickel-Catalyzed Coupling of Aryl Chlorides and Alcohols Under Thermal Conditions.
abstract: In search of more active and robust catalyst systems for the nickel-catalyzed coupling of aryl halides and heteroatom nucleophiles, a core scaffold modification of the conventional 2,2’-bipyridine ‘bpy’ ligand was explored. Transposition of one of the N-atom donors of bpy into the ligand backbone results in the isomeric bipyridine ligand ‘iso-bpy’, an N,Cdonor containing a highly electron-donating, strong-field 2-pyridylidene group.

title: Processing-and cell-stage thermodynamic screening of nacre-and bone-inspired carbonate and phosphate phases on aluminium current collectors in fluorine-free lithium-ion cells with an open screening framework
abstract: Water-processed, fluorine-free lithium-ion cathodes avoid fluorinated binders and organic solvents, but their alkaline slurry attacks the aluminium current collector, and the cell lacks the protective AlF3 layer that fluorinated salts form. Water-processed (bio-)binders do not protect the collector; the current fixes are pH control with H3PO4 and carbon-coated foil. We ask which nacre- and bone-lineage mineral phases can survive both the alkaline aqueous slurry and the oxidising potential of a fluorine-free cell, and which measurements would decide the rest.

title: Poly(pentafulvalene)s: One-Dimensional Conjugated Hydrocarbons toward Stable and Narrow-Bandgap Polyenes
abstract: Polyacetylene is the archetypal narrow-bandgap conjugated polymer, yet its high-lying HOMO renders it air-sensitive, and aromatic alternatives sacrifice the small bandgap inherent to a polyene backbone. Here we show that embedding the polyene in a dibenzopentafulvalene (DBF) framework affords a stable, narrow-bandgap polyene analog. Poly(dibenzopentafulvalene) (polyDBF) was synthesized by Kosugi–Migita–Stille polycondensation; its thin film absorbed up to 995 nm (optical bandgap 1.25 eV) and, unlike polyacetylene, persisted for days in air.

title: Lactonization of Acyloxy Radicals
abstract: Carboxylic acids have been used extensively as weak nucleophiles in lactonization and esterification processes involving activated electrophiles. Conversion of these building blocks into carboxyl radicals furnishes reactive species that are electrophilic in character but susceptible to decarboxylation. This high propensity for fragmentation, assessed to proceed at rates of 10 9-11 s -1 in the case of acyloxy radicals, has facilitated access to carbon radicals but impeded exploration of umpolung C–O bond forming reactions through non-decarboxylative pathways.

title: Shell-nested virtual spaces from atomic natural orbitals
abstract: Selecting a compact molecular virtual space requires deciding which radial and angular freedom can be removed while retaining a useful description of electron correlation. A correlated molecular density can guide this choice, but obtaining it requires a preliminary correlation calculation. Here we examine whether tabulated atomic natural orbitals (ANOs) can provide radial guidance within the previously introduced shell-nested framework.

title: Stepwise Condensation to Diversify Cyano-Substituted Vinylene-Linked COFs for Boosting H2O2 Photosynthesis
abstract: Driven by growing demand for structural diversification and practical application of vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs), it is critical to develop sustainable routes to monomers with highly tunable connectivity and functionality. Herein, we report an efficient route to a new class of aromatic DCP derivatives (DCP = 2,6-dimethyl-3,5-dicyanopyridine) via Hantzsch-type condensation from low-cost commodity chemicals.

title: Chemical Editing of DNA-Mediated Nanoparticle Superlattices through a CRISPR-inspired Strategy
abstract: Biological systems employ molecular machinery to organize matter into functional structures and dynamically modify their organization in response to external signals. Translating such capabilities into synthetic nanomaterials requires strategies to selectively modify the interactions that define their structure. DNAbased assembly exploits sequence-specific molecular recognition to organize nanoscale components into prescribed architectures, yet post-assembly modification of structural DNA bonds remains challenging.

title: Ladderane as a Saturated Bioisostere of ortho-Benzene
abstract: Previously, we proposed a hypothesis that ladderanes could mimic ortho-benzene in bioactive compounds. In this work, we have proven this hypothesis experimentally. In particular, 2,3-disubstituted ladderanes were efficiently synthesized and extensively characterized. These cores were then incorporated into six bioactive compounds instead of the benzene ring. The corresponding patent-free ladderane derivatives of Thalidomide and Oxatomide showed improved physicochemical profiles and similar biological activities compared to those of the original drugs.

title: A Pharmacophore-Based Virtual Screening Approach for the Discovery of Novel P2Y 12 Receptor Ligands
abstract: Microglia play key roles in neuroinflammation, which is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease and Multiple Sclerosis. To strengthen our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of these disorders, we need to understand the complex dynamics in microglial states. Developing new positron emission tomography (PET) tracers is exceptionally useful for this purpose, as they enable the assessment of microglia dynamics and function in the living human brain.
authors: Anne van der Schatte van der Schatte Olivier

title: SandCat: OpenMM Framework for Prospective Cryptic Pocket Discovery
abstract: Proteins are dynamic biomolecules, yet often in drug discovery they are treated as static entities. A relevant example of this are cryptic pockets, which are pockets that are not present in the apo structure but reveal themselves upon binding to a particular ligand. Methods based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can dynamically probe the protein structure and have been validated on known cryptic pocket sites. SWISH-X is one of the most prominent methods in this field. Previously, it was only available with GROMACS and PLUMED, which limited its speed.

title: Multinuclear High-Field FlowNMR for Real-Time Monitoring and Analysis of Biocatalytic Reactions in Batch and Flow
abstract: Online high-field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in continuous or recirculating flow (FlowNMR) offers a powerful yet underutilised approach for monitoring biocatalytic reactions, particularly in challenging aqueous and low-concentration systems. Herein, we demonstrate the application of multinuclear high-resolution FlowNMR at 500 MHz for real-time analysis of both batch and continuous flow biotransformations.

title: Disentangling protein confinement from surface adsorption in hierarchical zirconium metal-organic frameworks
abstract: A persistent challenge in protein immobilization within metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is distinguishing genuine internal confinement from surface adsorption and interparticle voids, which can mimic encapsulation despite fundamentally different spatial microenvironments. Incorporating mesochannels to produce hierarchical UiO-66-NH 2 and MOF-808 nanoparticles, prepared by micelle templating, offers a strategy to overcome this ambiguity while preserving their intrinsic microporosity.

title: Automated Full-Spectrum Multivariate Calibration for Quantitative Glow Discharge Optical Emission Spectrometry
abstract: Glow discharge optical emission spectrometry (GD-OES) enables rapid bulk and depthresolved multi-elemental analysis of solid materials with minimal sample preparation. Conventional quantification, however, relies on preselected analyte emission lines and, if sputtering-rate variations must be compensated, on matrix reference lines or sputtering-rate correction, requiring matrix composition or sputtering rates as input.

title: Tight binding of optically innocent bisphosphonate ligands to robust Tb3+-doped HfO2 nanocrystal surfaces
abstract: Lanthanide (Ln3+)-doped nanocrystals feature photostable, long-lived emission, making them attractive probes for in vitro and in vivo imaging. Their translation, however, hinges on a surface chemistry that confers colloidal stability under physiological conditions without compromising their photophysical properties. Here, we benchmark three classes of PEGylated anchoring groups—nitrocatecholates, phosphonates and bisphosphonates—on core and core/shell Tb3+-doped HfO2 nanocrystals.

title: From Azirinyl Radicals to Azirinium Cations: Small-Ring N-Heterocyclic Reactive Intermediates
abstract: Late-stage functionalization via reactive intermediates has recently emerged as an efficient way to access structurally diverse small rings, as illustrated with cyclopropyl radicals or cyclopropenium cations, which have opened valuable new synthetic opportunities. Their nitrogen counterparts, however, remain underexplored despite the importance of heterocycles in synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Dual Construction of peri-(C–C) and (C–N)/(N–N) Atropisomerism via C–H Activation
abstract: Axially chiral biaryls bearing an atropisomeric C–C axis at peri-substituted positions are difficult to access, and this difficulty compounds when the same scaffold must also carry a second, independent C–N or N–N axis, a combination that remains largely unexplored. Here we report an efficient, cost-effective route to these dual-axial atropisomers through enantioselective Co(II)/Salox-catalyzed C–H/N–H annulation. Arylbenzamide substrates bearing two distinct classes of directing groups react with peri-substituted alkynes to install both stereogenic axes in a single step.

title: Intramolecular Hydride Migration Enables Ring Substitution in a Diphosphacyclobutadienyl Complex
abstract: While substitution reactions at coordinated carbocyclic π-ligands are well established, similar examples of direct substitution at the ring carbon atoms of mixed carbon-phosphorus π-systems have remained scarce, owing to the intrinsic bias towards P-centered reactivity. Herein, we report a hydride-for-phosphonium substitution at a coordinated phosphorus heterocyclic π-system: protonation of the complex [W(CO)3{η 4-(PPh3)2C2P2}] bearing a zwitterionic diphosphacyclobutadienyl ligand affords a tungsten hydride complex which undergoes a selective rearrangement to [W(CO)3(PPh3){η…

title: Machine Learning for NMR Observables Sensitive to Nuclear Quantum Effects
abstract: Nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) are essential for an accurate description of systems containing light elements. Their omission in classical simulations can lead to significant deviations between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements, particularly for nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observables that are highly sensitive to quantum nuclear motion.

title: Adaptive Hydration-Shell ML/MM Simulations Recover Full ML Accuracy in Biomolecular Conformational Description
abstract: Residue-specific backbone conformational preferences govern the conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins, yet their accurate description using classical force fields is limited by prescribed functional forms that cannot fully represent environment-dependent many-body interactions. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) learn complex atomic interactions directly from quantum-mechanical reference data, providing a systematic alternative to classical parameterisations.

title: Gold deposition on surfaces using small organic molecules: effects of preparation conditions on morphology and Raman response
abstract: Reduction and subsequent deposition of noble metals from simple salt solutions on solid surfaces remains challenging. We describe deposition of gold (nano)-particles from an aqueous chloroauric adic solution on glass and polyethylene surfaces at ambient temperature by adding simple primordial organic molecules. The deposited gold structures showed differences in morphology, size and Raman response across the preparation conditions examined, motivating further investigation of their potential as functional surface coatings with distinct properties for various applications.

title: Chemical Synthesis and Immunological Evaluation of Archaeal Rare Sugar L-TalNAcA and Its Derivatives
abstract: Human-associated archaea, such as Methanobrevibacter smithii and Methanosphaera stadtmanae, have attracted increasing attention for their potential involvement in the modulation of host immune responses. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly understood. Pseudopeptidoglycan (pPG), a major component of the archaeal cell wall, is a potential mediator of such immunomodulatory effects.

title: Data-driven discovery and substrate scope mapping of dual-ligand nickel catalysts for C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-electrophile coupling
abstract: Dual-ligand nickel catalysis has emerged as an effective strategy for improving C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-electrophile coupling (XEC), yet the systematic studies identifying productive ligand combinations and mapping their target scope remain limited. In this work, we combine high-throughput experimentation (HTE) with a simple, interpretable data-analysis workflow to identify and validate synergistic bidentate–tridentate ligand pairs for Zn-mediated Ni-catalyzed XEC.

title: Tailoring Pt-CeO 2 Interactions to Bypass Activity-Selectivity Trade-Off for C 2 H 2 Semi-Hydrogenation
abstract: CeO 2 -supported platinum-group metals with small nanoparticles allow fine-tuning of their electronic properties through enhanced electronic interactions with the support. Here, we modify the electronic properties of a Pt/CeO 2 catalyst with 1.5 nm Pt nanoparticles by varying the near-surface oxygen vacancy concentration. In-situ infrared, X-ray photoelectron, and X-ray absorption spectroscopies show that roomtemperature oxidation followed by re-reduction at 100 o C decreases near-surface oxygen vacancies by ∼3-fold without altering Pt size, resulting in ∼25-fold increase in C 2 H 2…

title: A spectral law for blackbody radiation without temperature or Planck’s constant
Dynamics of oxygen and hydrogen species at the surface Ru/Al 2 O 3 revealed by advanced operando spectroscopies
abstract: The microscopic evolution of supported Ru-oxide nanoparticles under reducing conditions remains a central challenge in hydrogenation catalysis. In 5 wt% Ru/Al2O3 catalyst, the transformation of oxidized Ru species into metallic Ru, the formation of hydrides, and hydrogen exchange with the support are closely related but difficult to resolve simultaneously. Here, operando IR and O K-edge NEXAFS, supported by quantum chemical DFT calculations, show that the initially hydroxylated Ru-oxide surface contains *OOH and *OO-H species at unsaturated Ru sites characterized by a distinct O K-edge…

title: Controlled Competition Reduces Errors in Nanostructure-Based DNA Data Storage
abstract: DNA nanotechnology offers a promising route toward molecular data storage with exceptional density, longevity, and energy efficiency. Unlike sequence-based approaches that rely on large-scale synthesis and sequencing, structural DNA data storage encodes information into spatial architectures readable at the single-molecule level. However, practical implementation is hindered by substitution errors -particularly 0-to-1 “bit flips” - that arise during pooled readout and compromise data fidelity.

title: Targeted Covalent Inhibition of Pyk2 via a Paralog-Specific Cysteine for Selective Antiplatelet Action
abstract: Focal adhesion kinase 2 (FAK2, also known as Pyk2), a focal adhesion kinase (FAK) family member, has emerged as a promising antiplatelet target with minimal impact on normal hemostasis. However, the development of Pyk2-selective inhibitors has been constrained by limited paralog selectivity and suboptimal in vivo pharmacokinetics. Here, we report compound 2-1, a first-in-class covalent inhibitor that selectively targets Pyk2 by hijacking a unique cysteine residue (Cys545) absent in the sister kinase FAK1.

title: Beyond Atom Pairs: Multicenter Crystal Orbital Hamilton Populations for Molecules and Solids
abstract: The Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population (COHP) is a standard tool for energyresolved bonding analysis in solids and also applies to molecules, but it assigns the band energy only to atom pairs. A multicenter bond therefore has no energy of its own: across the five molecules and solids studied here, pairwise integrated COHP reports strong two-center bonding (−1.8 to −3.5 eV) and cannot distinguish an electrondeficient bridge from an electron-rich unit.

title: Helicene-Blade Molecular Propellers
abstract: Molecular propellers have attracted intense interest as a fascinating class of chiral molecules, as exemplified by hexaphenylbenzene derivatives bearing peripheral point-chiral substituents. However, these molecules typically show limited chiral configuration stability, hindering applications that require stable chiroptical responses. Herein, helicenes are introduced as blades to construct molecular propellers for the first time, achieving enhanced chiral stability.

title: Enhancing Interfacial Exciton Conversion in Blue Upconversion OLEDs through Oligomer-Controlled Molecular Orientation
abstract: Controlling molecular orientation is central to high-performance organic optoelectronics. Anthracene oligomers provide an orientation-tunable platform for elucidating orientation effects in upconversion organic light-emitting diodes (UC-OLEDs), which generate blue emission at exceptionally low driving voltages through interfacial charge-transfer (CT) states, CT-to-triplet (CT-to-T1) conversion, and triplet–triplet annihilation. Across anthracene derivatives, increasing horizontal orientation enhances external quantum efficiency (EQE) beyond that expected from light outcoupling alone.

title: Benchmarking a fast energy model for predicting the stability of solvated surface sites for organic molecular crystals: The paracetamol–water interface
abstract: Crystallisation of molecular materials is important for a range of industries including the pharmaceutical and agrochemical sectors. Prediction of the crystal growth and dissolution of such systems requires detailed knowledge of the thermodynamics, and ideally kinetics, of surface sites in contact with solvent. The most reliable method for obtaining the free energy of solvated kinks, step edges and terraces with molecular resolution is often via computer simulation using molecular dynamics, as this includes explicit solvent interactions and entropy changes, but comes at a significant…

title: Spatial Inhomogeneity of Thermal Degradation of Semi-Crystalline Polymers
abstract: The thermal degradation of polymers is typically interpreted as a uniform chemical process involving molecular weight reduction and oxidation. However, the role of localized microstructural changes as defect sites that deteriorate polymer mechanical performance remains underexplored owing to the limitations of conventional bulk characterization techniques. We applied an isotope-labeled Raman mapping technique with molecular weight selectivity to visualize the structural evolution of semi-crystalline polyethylene during long-term thermal exposure under conditions in which the bulk molecular…

title: Breaking Linear Scaling Relations for Regioselective Phenol Hydroxylation via SiC-Supported Dual-Atom Catalysts
abstract: The electrochemical hydroxylation of phenol offers a sustainable route to valueadded dihydroxybenzene isomers, yet rational catalyst design remains limited by 2 poor regioselectivity and structural instability. This study investigates silicon carbide (SiC) monoliths as exceptionally robust supports for dual-atom catalysts, utilizing density functional theory and operando ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to screen 45 bimetallic combinations.

title: Czochralski Growth of YSGAG Crystals: Experimental, Numerical, and Data-Assisted Analysis of Solid–Liquid Interface Shape
abstract: Yttrium scandium gallium aluminum garnet (YSGAG) is a promising diamagnetic substrate for yttrium iron garnet thin films, but scalable Czochralski growth requires control of the solid–liquid interface. Here, growth experiments, thermophysical-property measurements, and CGSim simulations are combined to analyze interface-shape control in YSGAG. The Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model was constrained and assessed using experimentally observed interface profiles from early, middle, and late stages of the constant-diameter regime.

title: Predicting Regulator-Listed N-Nitrosamines from API Structure: A Rule-Based Method with a Retrospectively Corrected FDA and EMA Evaluation
abstract: Regulator lists of N-nitrosamines include assessed and hypothetical impurities as well as detected compounds. We evaluate a deterministic rule-based method that proposes N-nitrosamine structures from an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) through direct nitrosation, selected nitrosative dealkylation pathways and nitrosation after one degradation step. The engine was refined against the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) list and frozen. An external European Medicines Agency (EMA) set excludes all FDA API identities using standardized parent connectivity.

title: Hybrid Joining Technologies for Composites: Mechanisms, Performance, Challenges, and Perspectives
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites are increasingly used in aircraft structures with their high specific strength, stiffness, corrosion resistance, and lightweight nature. However, reliably joining FRP components is challenging because mechanical joining can create stress concentrations, fiber damage, and delamination, while adhesive bonding can cause peel stress, environmental degradation, and inspection challenges.

title: Computational Exploration of Dopamine Adsorption on Carbon Nanotubes for Electrochemical Sensing
abstract: Dopamine (DA), has a variety of impacts on human health. Due to the high cost and labor-intensity of its current measurement methods, sensitive and low-cost electrochemical sensors with carbonaceous substrate materials have been proposed as an alternative. Single-chirality single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) have gained interest for their chirality-dependent properties. In a recent study, we demonstrated that the sensing response of DA varies for SWCNT chiralities.

title: Comparative Analysis of Basic Machine Learning and Rigorous Free-Energy Calculation on Benchmarking Datasets of Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity
abstract: Rigorous free-energy methods based on molecular dynamics simulations like free-energy perturbation (FEP) are nowadays widely applied in lead optimization in pharmaceutical companies. Due to sampling restrictions and potential force-field deficiencies, it is common practice to first validate the applicability of FEP to a target/chemical series using a small number of known compounds, before applying it prospectively.

title: Polymer interface-driven perovskite crystallization in electrospun fibers
abstract: Polymer incorporation into metal halide perovskite films is an effective strategy to control perovskite nucleation and crystallization, passivate defects and suppress humidity-induced degradation. In this work, we use enthalpic interactions between insulating polymers and formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI 3 ) to control FAPbI 3 crystal size, quality and location.

title: Regime-Switching Control of C–N Bond Evolution in Electrochemical Methylamine Oxidation
abstract: Electrochemical amine oxidation typically involves competing pathways that govern the fate of C–N bonds, yet selective control over bond preservation, cleavage, and reconstruction remains challenging. Here we demonstrate the first single-substrate electrochemical system enabling switchable synthesis of formamide and N-methylformamide from methylamine as a model amine. Product selectivity can be reversibly switched by independently varying anodic potential, electrolyte composition, or methylamine concentration.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: The Current Roles of AI in Public Health Practice: Scoping Review
abstract: BackgroundAI is a broad field encompassing various techniques, which include algorithms that learn from data to perform automated tasks without explicit human programming. Public health aims to protect and improve the health of communities and populations at the local, regional, national, and global levels, but it typically has limited resources. While AI may lead to improved efficiency or effectiveness of public health interventions, the adoption of AI interventions should be informed by evidence of effective use in practice.ObjectiveThis review aims to summarize how AI-assisted…

title: Visible-Light-Driven Dehydrogenative Ketone Synthesis from Unprotected Primary Alcohols and Aryl Bromides
abstract: Owing to their widespread natural abundance, alcohols are regarded as highly attractive coupling partners in organic synthesis. Although O–H or C–O activating cross-couplings of alcohols have been well-established in distinct contexts, the direct C–H oxidative coupling of alcohols to form ketones remains rare. Herein, we disclose a visible-light-driven, bromine-radical-mediated hydrogen-atom-transfer/nickel relay that enables the direct conversion of unprotected primary alcohols and aryl bromides to aryl alkyl ketones under ambient conditions.

title: Ensemble RMSD-Driven Metadynamics for Electrolyte-Reduction Pathway Discovery
Machine Learning-Guided Design of Cu-Based Single-Atom Alloy Nanoclusters for Selective CO2 Electroreduction
abstract: Metal nanoclusters are highly promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (eCO2RR) due to their abundant low-coordination sites and size-dependent electronic properties. Alloying these clusters with isolated transition metal atoms to form Cu-based single-atom alloys (Cu-SAAs) provides a powerful strategy to finely tune their local structures and electronic properties. Because the dopant element identifies and its specific surface site strongly dictate *CO adsorption and subsequent eCO2RR pathways, systematically mapping this combinatorial space is critical.

title: Data-Driven Analysis of C–F Bond Lengths in Two-Dimensional Fluorinated Carbon Materials
abstract: The C–F bond length is an important structural descriptor of fluorinated carbon materials, but its reported values remain widely scattered across the literature. Here, a compilation and statistical analysis of C–F bond lengths is presented, focusing on two-dimensional (2D) fluorinated carbon materials and comparing them with fluorinated low-dimensional and molecular systems. The 2D dataset comprises 176 entries spanning C0.86F to C200F and covering publications from 1934 to 2026.

title: Metal-Organic Frameworks as Single-Particle Contrast Agents for Localization Optoacoustic Tomography
abstract: Localization optoacoustic tomography (LOT) resolves microvascular networks beyond the acoustic diffraction limit by detecting and tracking individual absorbing particles in the bloodstream. Single-particle detection in LOT remains challenging for clinically acceptable contrast materials, typically requiring particle diameters of ~5 μm to overcome the strong absorption background of blood. Here, we show that metal-organic framework (MOF) microparticles overcome this limitation.

title: Multi-Scale Light-Based Biofabrication of Acrylate-Free Magnetic Gelatin Composites for Transient Vascular Navigation
abstract: Photocurable hydrogels derived from native proteins offer high bio-functionality for biomedical micro-devices; however, traditional approaches require chemical functionalization such as methacrylation, altering native bio-activity. Here, an acrylate-free photocurable magnetic composite ink is developed using native gelatin photocrosslinked via ruthenium-mediated di-tyrosine coupling and loaded with zinc-substituted iron oxide (ZFO) nanoparticles.

title: Toward the Synthesis of Verteporfin from Hemin and Protoporphyrin IX
abstract: This report describes two approaches toward verteporfin (benzoporphyrin derivative monoacid), a photosensitizer used in photodynamic therapy. One starts from hemin and the other from commercial protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). The hemin route first converts hemin into PpIX dimethyl ester, by reductive removal of iron and concomitant acid-catalyzed esterification. The benzoporphyrin skeleton of verteporfin is then built from PpIX dimethyl ester by a Diels-Alder cycloaddition with dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD).

title: High-Performance Chemiresistive Humidity Sensing and Quantum Isotopic Differentiation with Single Crystals of a Conductive MOF Hosting Electron Spin Qubits
abstract: Conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a versatile platform for chemiresistive humidity sensing, a capability vital for industrial and biomedical applications. However, grain boundaries and uncontrolled crystallite orientations in commonly used polycrystalline devices limit sensing performance, while electrical responses alone lack specificity for distinguishing H2O from D2O.

title: Model Dependence and Cancellation in a Fixed-Geometry Lactone Energy Cycle
abstract: A small signed energy response can conceal larger individual changes and may not transfer between computational models. We compare fixed lactone and methanolysis-product conformers through a balanced eight-state protonation-response cycle. Existing density-functional calculations give gas and implicit-methanol cycles of +18.327235 and +4.381410 kJ/mol. Matched 0.020 Å H-only displacements lower every cation energy but change the solvent cycle by −0.072625 kJ/mol. The four-arm first-order force-work prediction is −0.237920 kJ/mol, with a signed finite-step remainder of +0.165294 kJ/mol.

title: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
abstract: The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Operando Surface Dynamics Govern the pH-Universal Activity and Stability of Cobalt Phosphide for Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Cobalt phosphide (CoP) has been established as a highly promising, pH-universal electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the operando surface structure–activity relationship and the mechanistic origins of its high stability remain elusive. Here, we combine large-scale data mining (2,282 experimental observations), surface Pourbaix diagrams, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and microkinetic modeling to reveal the operando surface configurations of CoP. We demonstrate that at low overpotentials (<100 mV), the surface is dominated by HO*-covered configurations featuring P–OH groups. This P–OH enrichment critically modulates the electronic structure of adjacent Co active sites, optimizing H* adsorption and facilitating water activation. At high overpotentials (>100 mV), the surface undergoes a structural transition to a dense H* coverage (comprising Co–H and P–H species), which maintains highly favorable adsorption thermodynamics of H* near the Sabatier optimum (ΔGH* = 0 eV) across the wide pH range of 0–14 under the applied electric field. Surface coverage mapping and 2D microkinetic volcano analyses, using ΔGHO* and ΔGH* as key descriptors, further corroborate these potential-dependent surface species and the resulting high HER activity. Crucially, these potential-dependent surface adsorbates protect CoP from detrimental element leaching. Moreover, comprehensive experimental characterizations validate our theoretical predictions. This work exemplifies the capabilities of combining AI-driven data platforms with precise simulations in accelerating scientific discoveries and uncovering underlying catalytic mechanisms.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
abstract: Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MedMLX: On-Device Medical Imaging AI for Apple Silicon
abstract: Background: Medical imaging research increasingly combines specialized artificial intelligence models for segmentation, detection, image synthesis and report generation. For three-dimensional CT and MRI, these workflows typically run on NVIDIA GPUs with substantial memory. On-device AI on widely available Apple Silicon computers could broaden access to these models for clinical researchers. These computers share a large memory pool between the CPU and GPU, which suits workflows that combine several models. However, few established imaging models run natively on Apple Silicon.

title: Leadership Development Programmes for Clinical Nurses: A Systematic Review
abstract: AimTo provide a comprehensive understanding of the current leadership development programmes for clinical nurses.DesignSystematic review was designed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines.Data sourcesFour electronic databases from 2014 to 2026 studies published were searched.MethodsA comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus and Web of Science. title: Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy
abstract: Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: High Temperature Stable Pt Nanoclusters Formation in Alumina-Encapsulated Pt Catalysts
abstract: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics.

title: Reinforcement Learning with World Models in the Era of Scale: From Online Imagination to World Action Models
abstract: In World Model Reinforcement Learning (WM-RL), agents learn a parameterized model of environmental dynamics that serves as the basis for planning, imagination-based policy training, or synthetic data generation in decision making tasks. From 2019 to 2026, a drastic phase transition took place within this field. Initially started as an effort to improve efficiency in visual control tasks, WM-RL has become the core of interdisciplinary AI infrastructure.

title: Theoretical characterization of hydroxyfuranones related to biomass burning and their tautomers
Bioinspired Proton–Electron Dual Channels for Selective Photocatalytic Oxidation of Methane to Methanol
abstract: Photocatalytic methane conversion holds great promise for upgrading this abundant feedstock under ambient conditions, yet the selective partial oxidation of methane to methanol remains challenging. In triphasic aerobic photocatalysis, inefficient interfacial supply and transfer of protons and electrons restrict methanol production and promote overoxidation. Herein, we design bioinspired proton–electron dual-channels on the photocatalyst through surface modification with trimesic acid and palladium.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Néel vector switching by magnetization-dependent layer-resolved spin-orbit torque
abstract: Layer-resolved spin-orbit torques offer a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order through local spin-charge conversion. First-principles calculations show that the layer-resolved spin Hall conductivity of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator $\mathrm{Mn{Bi}_{2}{Te}_{4}}$ consists of a magnetization-independent spin Hall term plus two spin anomalous Hall terms that are even in the Néel vector yet evolve with the local magnetic order, while local inversion asymmetry differentiates surface and inner layers. This response enables reversible, field-free switching of the Néel vector in finite-septuple-layer films. Although the magnetization-independent spin Hall term alone can reverse the order, the spin anomalous Hall terms provide magnetization-dependent feedback that redistributes the layer-resolved torques and reshapes the switching trajectory, offering a route to tailoring current-driven switching through layer and interface engineering.

title: Reaction precedents extend retrosynthetic prediction beyond training coverage
abstract: Reaction precedents guide retrosynthesis, but how far they can compensate for gaps in task-specific training coverage remains unclear. Using 2.71 million reactions, we restricted training and retrieval coverage by transformation or time, then expanded only the retrieval corpus with model parameters fixed. For transformations excluded from training, mean Top-1 accuracy increased from 13.0% to 58.0% on a historical test set and from 4.9% to 23.1% on a temporally held-out test set. For temporal coverage gaps, retrieval expansion enabled a model trained on records before 2017 to match or exceed a non-retrieval model trained on records before 2025 on both test sets. Without task-specific fine-tuning, precedents improved all 14 representative general-purpose models on both test sets and USPTO-50K; the strongest with precedents surpassed all eight representative specialized models. These findings show that inference-time reaction precedents can extend retrosynthetic prediction beyond task-specific training coverage without parameter updates.

title: Unweaving the mechanics of woven fabrics through automated model discovery
abstract: Woven fabrics have multiple structural, aesthetic, and medical applications that require knowledge of their mechanical properties. While isolated fiber properties are easily determined, bulk properties of woven material, which can be coated or locally reinforced, require knowledge of yarn density, weave style, and other characteristics that are difficult to obtain experimentally. Additionally, fiber rearrangement, twist, yarn contact, and fiber-direction coupling result in non-linear mechanical responses. As a result, there is no universal material model for woven materials, and each fabric requires a specific model and parameter calibration. Recently, methods to simultaneously discover material models and their parameters from experimental or synthetic datasets have been proposed. Here, we use automated model discovery to simultaneously extract the material model and its parameters from biaxial test data of a TPU-coated woven nylon fabric. We show that Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks discover a sparse three-term hyperelastic material law with one isotropic and two anisotropic contributions, reproducing the measured biaxial response with a mean $R^2=0.97$. Across 20 initializations, predictive accuracy remains robust despite variations in the exact sparse representation, consistent with strong correlations between several candidate terms. LARS-LASSO independently recovers the same dominant constitutive contributions at approximately 100-fold lower computational cost. These results are directly applicable to numerical finite-element models of fabric-based structures, including soft robotic devices. More broadly, these results provide a foundation for further model discovery, improved constitutive modeling, and mechanistically informed optimization of woven fabric structures.

title: From MS/MS evidence to adaptive spectroscopic characterization: Reinforcement learning guided by candidate molecular structures
abstract: Small-molecule identification from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) may require complementary measurements. Herein, we propose a structure-informed deep Q-network (SI-DQN) that uses existing MS/MS evidence to decide whether further characterization is needed, which measurement to request, and when to stop. The policy combines spectral representations and candidate rankings with score-weighted descriptors of the candidates' chemical features and structural differences. The policy was evaluated on 79,462 held-out samples with simulated MS/MS, infrared (IR), and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra from the Multimodal Spectroscopic Dataset. Evaluation used fixed hard candidate sets containing the correct structure and equal normalized acquisition costs. Averaged across three training runs, SI-DQN increased Top-1 accuracy from 80.10% to 93.78% for positive-ion MS/MS starts and from 70.44% to 93.31% for negative-ion starts. The corresponding mean additional measurement counts were only 0.227 and 0.340 per sample, respectively. Complete acquisition achieved 97.72% accuracy with four additions, whereas SI-DQN reduced the additional measurement count by 94.3% and 91.5%. Relative to a rule-based policy, SI-DQN reduced the composite loss combining terminal ranking error and acquisition cost by 19.3% and 25.5%. Adding structural information to DQN further improved accuracy while reducing requests across all three training runs. At comparable ranking uncertainty, SI-DQN increased request rates relative to DQN more strongly in groups with high structural disagreement, where larger reductions in composite loss were also observed. Together, these results support using the ambiguity among candidate structures after MS/MS analysis to guide further characterization, providing a quantitative basis for balancing identification performance against subsequent measurement effort.

title: Topological Quantum Spin Liquids in a Ladder with Majorana fermions and p-wave Superconductivity
abstract: In this article, we address the possibility of topological quantum spin liquids with only short-range (spin) correlations in the whole phase diagram in a ladder system, through an exactly solvable model which represents a generalization of the two-dimensional Kitaev honeycomb spin model to a ribbon geometry. This system gives rise to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge fields emerging in a static way in the ground state through Majorana fermions which then produce either $0$ or $π$ flux. Through a quantum field theory perspective, mathematical and Density Matrix Renormalization Group results, we present our progress on the geometrical, topological and physical classification of this model through observables navigating on the whole phase diagram presenting three spin-liquid phases with a spin gap and a metallic phase in the sense of Majorana fermions. We propose a bulk-edge correspondence revealing the presence of protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edge in the phases with a gap and revealing also the presence of itinerant Majorana fermions in the bulk in the topological liquid phase. The proposed approach allows us to distinguish between properties of the brickwall ladder giving rise to a special line and those of the square ladder allowing for the gapless Majorana liquid phase. This model gives some hope on finding solutions for topological quantum spin models, e.g. with $π$ flux, on a square lattice geometry. This approach also allows for a correspondence onto models of topological superconductivity.

title: Large Magnetocaloric Effect and Adiabatic Temperature Change in the Tellurate: Gd2TeO6
abstract: We investigate the structural, magnetic, thermodynamic, and magnetocaloric properties of polycrystalline Gd2TeO6, a rare-earth tellurate unexplored for cryogenic magnetic refrigeration. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms single-phase orthorhombic symmetry (P212121), featuring two crystallographically distinct seven-coordinate Gd sites. Magnetization measurements reveal no conventional long-range magnetic ordering down to 2 K, although low-field magnetic irreversibility emerges below approximately 4 K. Curie-Weiss analysis yields a Weiss temperature of -1.25 K, indicating weak predominantly antiferromagnetic interactions. The magnetization reaches approximately 97% of the theoretical saturation moment at 7 T with negligible hysteresis. Heat-capacity measurements reveal no sharp zero-field anomaly above 2 K, while a broad field-induced maximum indicates redistribution of low-energy magnetic entropy. Debye-Einstein analysis separates the lattice and magnetic contributions. At 2.5 K, the maximum magnetic entropy changes (-DeltaSM) reach 21.40, 48.51, and 54.81 J kg-1 K-1 for field changes of 0-2, 0-5, and 0-7 T, respectively. The corresponding volumetric entropy change reaches 400.50 mJ cm-3 K-1. Measurements up to 14 T yield (-DeltaSM) = 63.51 J kg-1 K-1, approaching the theoretical limit of 64.25 J kg-1 K-1. The estimated adiabatic temperature change is approximately 22.7 K for 0-7 T. First-principles calculations with GGA+U approximation reveal competing antiferromagnetic states, highlighting Gd2TeO6 as a promising candidate for cryogenic magnetocaloric applications.

title: Data-Driven Approach for Predicting Long-Time Anomalous Transport from Short Trajectories
abstract: Molecular simulations provide detailed microscopic trajectories but often do not reach the long-time transport regime. Predicting long-time transport from ensembles of short trajectories is particularly challenging in heterogeneous materials, where static spatial disorder and viscoelastic memory can produce similar transient dynamics while leading to different behaviors at longer times.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Switching the Ordering Pattern of Bi2Rh4 Breathing Distortion by Isovalent Chalcogen Substitution in Bi2Rh3 X 2 ( X = Se, S)
abstract: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume.

title: Differentiable Electronic Grand Canonical Learning for Electrochemistry
abstract: Electronic grand-canonical density functional theory captures how structure and electronic charge respond to electrode potential and, together with statistical mechanics, how these responses give rise to emergent phenomena. However, its computational cost limits the system sizes and sampling times accessible to first- principles simulations. Here, we introduce a differentiable architecture that represents the grand potential and obtains forces and electronic charge as its derivatives, exactly satisfying the mixed-derivative constraints required for thermodynamic consistency, and implement it within the equivariant MACE framework as GC- MACE. We demonstrate more accurate joint learning across multiple electrochemical interfaces and improved transferability to thicker water films relative to previous models, while enabling constant-potential simulations at substantially larger length and time scales than accessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. With broad training data, the framework offers a route to thermodynamically consistent foundation interatomic potentials for the electronic grand canonical ensemble

title: Soliton-Lattice Origin of Incommensurability in High-Pressure Antimony
abstract: The microscopic origin of incommensurability in host-guest crystals remains unresolved. Here we show that the high-pressure antimony host-guest phase Sb-II is a soliton lattice, where localized guest-host misregistries decorate a commensurate 4/3 reference structure. First-principles calculations reveal a corrugated and hysteretic registry landscape, motivating a Frenkel-Kontorova description that accounts for soliton-lattice approximants of the form $(4n+1)/(3n+1)$. Machine-learning-potential calculations of these approximants show an energetically preferred soliton spacing, and their localized misregistry cores are also verified by first-principles relaxations. At finite temperature, the thermally broadened soliton lattice appears as an atomic density wave along the guest chains, consistent with experimental diffraction. This soliton-registry picture provides a microscopic mechanism for host-guest incommensurability in Sb-II.
